title: A Broke Blacksmith Just Learned A Legendary Sword Dance By Staring At A Wall . . . (Episode 7)
caption:
In Overgeared episode 7, Grid gambles his best loot on weapon upgrades, and finds Pagma's hidden mural.
A legendary sword dance is his, but the Yatan army is coming. Follow for episode 8!

#overgeared #anime #animerecap #animeexplained #fyp
comment: Would you have saved the bullies from the spider, or left them in the web? Why?

segments.say: A broke blacksmith just stared at a cave wall for three hours and walked out with a legendary *sword dance*.
To see how it got here, go back to Grid, who barely *survived* his first boss raid.
He got none of the sylphid scales he wanted, but he did walk away with a pile of *loot*.
The best part is a handful of blessed enhancement stones, which soften the penalty when a weapon *fails*.
Grid hugs one like it's his *baby*.
But his family is still drowning in *debt*, and every single yen counts.
So of course he spends a thousand gold on ten more enhancement *stones*.
He calls it an investment. Then he hits *enhance*.
Plus one, plus two, plus three, and he is already up to plus *five*.
That was his first mistake.
Past plus six, the odds fall off a *cliff*, and Grid knows it.
He pushes anyway. The enhancement fails, the penalty hits, and his dagger drops back *down*.
But luck turns, and soon his dagger blazes at plus *six*.
He strolls into town and the crowd *gawks*.
Then a rich rival named Roy shoves his own huge *sword* in Grid's face.
Roy paid for his weapon. Grid *made* his own.
Roy just laughs and calls him a broke *loser*.
Grid shrugs it off and swears he will never touch his best *stones*. Sure he won't.
Back at the forge, Khan has gone back to the anvil and made Grid a set of epic *armor*.
The old smith says it might be the greatest thing his hands have ever *made*.
Grid is so pumped he forgets all about Roy and his *sword*.
Now he marches into Kasong Canyon, hunting a mural of Pagma's sword *dance*.
He is only level eighty-five, and the lizardmen here are level one sixty-*two*.
But Khan's armor cuts the damage, and one swing drops a monster twice his *level*.
A whole pack swarms him, so he blocks, and unleashes a big *combo*.
A lucky double hit later, the whole pack is *down*.
Nearly a million experience points for one fight. Not bad for a *blacksmith*.
But the real trouble is still *ahead*.
The canyon has worse things than lizardmen, like a giant spider with way too many *eyes*.
Then he hears shouting. Three players are stuck in its *web*.
Grid freezes. He knows these guys. They bullied Takumi all through high *school*.
His first instinct is to run *away*.
Then he stops. He is not that weak kid *anymore*.
He walks back and offers to help, and his helmet hides his *face*.
Then his eyes light up. This is his chance for *revenge*.
He will cut them loose, but only for all of their *money*.
They figure out he is just mocking them, and one gets right in his *face*.
So Grid answers with a childish chant and dances around them like a *clown*.
It felt good for about five *seconds*.
One of them, the guy who once told the others to quit, asks him to *stop*.
But none of them will beg. They would rather die than grovel to *him*.
Grid storms off, and he feels worse than *ever*.
Even in the one place he gets to be a badass, they can still make him feel *small*.
So he turns back to watch the spider eat them. But they have already logged *out*.
Instead, the spider comes for *him*.
His blade wind bounces off its armor, and he cannot get *close*.
So he mixes two skills together, and it *clicks*.
A brand-new fusion skill, Wind of Justice, rips the beast *apart*.
Level eighty-six. But he is not alone out *there*.
A ragged stranger steps out of the dark and offers him an S-rank *quest*.
The target is Asmophel, a red knight who framed him and drove him out of the *castle*.
Grid says no. He has no time and no strength for a side *quest*.
Then the stranger dangles his own sword as a *reward*.
Grid tells him to go ahead and kill him, because failing a quest is *worse*.
The stranger just tells him to get lost. He does not kill the *innocent*.
So Grid goes back to the only thing that matters, the *mural*.
Behind a waterfall, a hidden cave glows. And there it *is*.
But the quest will not clear, so he copies the dance for three *hours*.
Then the system pings. Quest *clear*.
He just earned Pagma's sword dance, with twenty percent more attack and a bonus to fatal *hits*.
He needs more mana to use all of it, but he already feels like a *combat* class.
But far away, the Yatan army is closing in on a *fortress*.
A knight warns that it will arrive in days, and only one man could have planned *it*.
Dread incarnate, High Priest *Malaxus*.
